design.noise_seed_rule: First eight SHA-256 bytes, unsigned big endian, of compact ASCII JSON: [base,"paired",pair_id,phase,E1,E2], [base,"isolated",component_id,phase,E], or [base,"empty",phase,zero_based_repeat]. The paired noise timeline is reused across delays for the same combination.
design.selection: Choose nearest eligible point to each fixed geometric target in units of 0.4 x pitch, 0.4 y pitch and 5 mm depth, ties by saved reference. No waveform features enter selection. Qualified points have complete native endpoints and distinct coordinates outside the training point set.
design.matching: One-to-one chronological matching within ±60 ns of each arrival plus its phase- and energy-matched noiseless isolated trigger offset. Maximize matched count, minimize total absolute error, break ties in event order. If that reference is missing, anchor to the physical onset. Strip IDs and energy never enter matching.
design.trigger_success: Exactly two reconstructed triggers, both matched at a nonzero input delay. An unmatched trigger is false under this scoring rule. A sole matched trigger leaves two-to-one overlap or a suppressed trigger unresolved. A single merged trigger can still include multiple collecting strips. Electrode-local pileup uses the readout flags and is counted separately from the global trigger merge.
design.feature_success: Require two distinct triggers and correct X/Y strip identities, then a qualified slow energy or two calibrated lateral coordinates on each event. Tolerance success further requires the corresponding isolated reference values. Report truth bias independently of those relative tolerances.
design.metric_denominators: Per-trial criteria use all preset paired windows. Axis and pulse counts use the two true pulses per paired window or one per isolated window. Bias summaries use only matched pulses with the stated observable and reference available. Energy, XY and fast feature biases require the correct collecting pixel and two resolved triggers in a paired window. Unresolved windows retain the trigger census and any single-trigger total bias.
design.stability: Require complete success in every trial at the quoted delay and every later sampled delay, for at least three sampled delays. This defines a finite-grid result.

electronics.phase: Common ADC phase in ns, 0 <= phase < one sample period, relative to acquisition time zero.
electronics.analog: Sum exact two-pole responses to signed piecewise-constant native currents. Verified endpoints allow free decay.
electronics.adc: Add nominal independent noise once per complete sampled channel if seeded, then quantize once.
electronics.trigger: Coincident positive increments of both signed all-contact face sums from the continuous fast branch.
electronics.trigger_reference: Last sample before coincident rise activity, following at least three quiet increments to rearm.
electronics.strip_assignment: Positive net step on one strip per face after trigger settling, with fixed GeGI strip-pair compatibility.
electronics.unresolved_scope: One observed rise may contain multiple interactions. Its measured amplitude does not resolve that multiplicity.
electronics.slow_scope: Continuous nominal trapezoid and fixed pulser gain. Report the mean of an independently qualified X/Y pair.
electronics.fast_scope: Nominal signed 240 ns area with subtraction of the recent quiet fast level. Position is a nominal calibration transfer to the ADC trigger reference.
electronics.local_interference: For each other observed rise, project its measured pole-zero activity and settled charge step into this electrode’s slow trapezoid and locally referenced fast and timing gates. Screen affected observables without subtracting predicted interference.

design.scope: Fixed current superpositions of independently saved point injections in one nominal field. ADC noise is synthetic Gaussian noise and does not represent instrument data. Energy scaling uses linear native charge. Detector response and calibration use one simulated model. Millimeter XY requires supported calibration, leaving remote coordinates null. Fast observables compare to isolated waveforms, with no independent fast-area truth. Depth is unscored.
